title: Upgrade Sentry: sampled regression checks for catalog & tenant-locked versions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: When a model version is pinned or upgraded (either in the global catalog or a tenant-locked pin), regressions in generation quality can silently degrade customer experiences. Existing hooks are heavy-weight and either run too frequently (cost) or too slowly (miss early regressions).

Goal: Implement 'Upgrade Sentry' — an automated, cost-aware sampled evaluation pipeline that triggers on catalog and tenant pin/upgrade events to detect quality regressions quickly and surface deterministic alerts to owners. This is intended to be a lightweight, prioritized, and tenant-aware layer that complements our heavier preflight and canary machinery.

Success metrics:
- Detect regression signal (delta in key eval metrics) within 30 minutes of a pin event for high-priority tenants.
- False positive rate for alerts < 5% over a rolling 14-day window.
- Average cost per pin-eval event < $X (budget target; engineering to validate).
- 80% of alerted regressions include a reproducible sample and initial triage tags (quality, prompt-type, model-diff).
acceptance_criteria: A webhook/listener triggers sampled-eval jobs for both catalog and tenant pin events
Sampling strategy supports tenant-priority and traffic-aware weights
Evaluation jobs run within a sandboxed orchestration with cost caps and timeouts
Regression scoring compares new vs. baseline with configurable thresholds and returns a triage payload (examples, delta metrics, confidence)
Alerting integration emits signals to Console (rollout timeline) and Slack on high-confidence regressions
Runbook created for on-call + owner actions including immediate rollback and escalation path
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal opt-in): wire event hook into model-pin API, run sampled checks for catalog pins only, surface results to a private Console view and a #eval-sentry Slack channel. Phase 2 (tenant-priority): enable tenant-locked pin events, introduce tenant weighting and cost budgets, add per-tenant sampling knobs. Phase 3 (guard rails): automatic canary hold/flag when regression score exceeds threshold and owner validation absent. Each phase gated behind perf/cost validation and a small pilot group.
monitoring_and_alerting: Expose metrics: pin_event_count, sampled_eval_jobs_started, median_eval_latency, regression_alert_rate, avg_cost_per_pin_eval. Alerts: P0 if high-confidence regression for enterprise tenants (page on-call), P1 for catalog low-confidence regressions (notify owners). Console dashboard will show per-pin timeline, example inputs/outputs, and metric delta visualization.
implementation_notes: Sampling: combine traffic-derived sampling (recent request distribution), tenant priority (enterprise vs free), and deterministic seed-based sample for reproducibility
Baseline selection: prefer most-recent-stable pin or last-promoted catalog version; fallback to historical median on low-traffic tenants
Cost controls: per-eval token cap, execution timeout, and a global budget throttle with soft-fail (queue) and hard-fail behaviors
Security: only run synthetic probes in customer-safe mode (no real PII prompts); if tenant permits customer-prompt sampling, require opt-in and KMS enforcement
Observability: record request/response hashes, model fingerprint, quantization/variant metadata for triage
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy alerts from natural distribution drift — Mitigation: use rolling baselines and ensemble metrics (semantic similarity + ngram + human-calibrated scores)
Risk: cost explosion for high churn catalogs — Mitigation: progressive backoff, per-release budget caps, and differential sampling
Risk: slow feedback for low-traffic tenants — Mitigation: allow tenant-scoped synthetic probe templates and weighted sampling
Risk: false-positive regression detection on benign metric variance — Mitigation: require multi-metric confirmation and optional manual verification step prior to automatic rollback
notes: Request from customer success: several enterprise tenants asked for earlier regression signals during a recent catalog rollout (Feb 2026)
This feature should interoperate with existing preflight/canary tooling but be simpler and lower-latency
Estimate and cost target are provisional; engineering to validate during spike
